title: Absolute Difference Between Maximum and Minimum K Elements
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, determine the absolute difference between the sum of the k largest elements and the sum of the k smallest elements in the array.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, determine the absolute difference between the sum of the k largest elements and the sum of the k smallest elements in the array. Return this difference as an integer.
constraints: Compare the sum of the k largest elements with the sum of the k smallest elements.
Return their absolute difference; elements are chosen by position, including duplicates.
hints: The minimum k-element sum uses the k smallest values; the maximum uses the k largest.
Sort once to expose both groups.
Subtract the first-k sum from the last-k sum.
An exchange argument shows replacing any chosen value by a more extreme available value can only improve its respective sum.
editorial: An exchange argument shows replacing any chosen value by a more extreme available value can only improve its respective sum.

tests.explanation: The largest pair sums to nine and the smallest pair to four, giving five.
Every two-element selection has the same sum, so the difference is zero.
